rows.answer: Section 4 imposes income tax on the taxable income of every person who has taxable income for the tax year. The tax is levied at the rate or rates specified in Division I or Division II of Part I of the First Schedule, as applicable to the taxpayer, for tax year 2027 onward.

rows.answer: For tax year 2027 onwards, the surcharge under Section 4AB is levied at a rate of ten percent of the income tax imposed under Division I of Part I of the First Schedule. It applies only when a person’s taxable income exceeds Rs 10 million, and no surcharge is payable on income chargeable under the head “Salary”.

rows.answer: Overtime payments and bonuses are included in the definition of salary and therefore are taxable under the head “Salary”. Section 12(2)(a) expressly lists overtime payment and bonus among the amounts that constitute salary for tax purposes. This applies for the tax year 2027 onward.

rows.answer: A car that an employer provides to an employee for private use is treated as a taxable perquisite and its value is added to the employee’s salary under section 13(3) of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 [1]. The amount to be included is calculated according to Rule 5 of the Income Tax Rules 2002: if the car is used partly for personal purposes, 5 % of the employer’s cost (or the fair market value at lease commencement) is taken as the taxable value; if the car is used wholly for personal purposes, 10 % of the cost (or fair market value) is taken [2]. This applies for tax year 2027.

rows.answer: Under section 15, “rent” means any amount received or receivable by the owner of land or a building as consideration for the use or occupation of, or the right to use or occupy, that land or building, and it also includes any forfeited deposit paid under a contract for the sale of land or a building. The definition excludes rent received for the lease of a building together with plant and machinery, which is taxed under “Income from Other Sources”, and amounts included for amenities, utilities or other services connected with the renting of the building are also treated under “Income from Other Sources”.

rows.answer: For tax year 2027, foreign‑source income of a short‑term resident individual is exempt if (a) the person is resident in Pakistan only because of his employment, (b) he has been present in Pakistan for a period or periods not exceeding three years, and (c) the income is not derived from a business established in Pakistan and is not brought into or received in Pakistan. If either of the exceptions in sub‑section (2) applies – i.e., the income comes from a Pakistan‑based business or is received in Pakistan – the exemption does not apply. [1]

rows.answer: For tax year 2027, an unabsorbed business loss under the head “Income from Business” may be carried forward for a maximum of six successive tax years.  Exceptions apply: a loss of a government‑owned banking company approved by the State Bank can be carried forward for ten years; a loss of a resident hotel business can be carried forward for eight years; and a loss of Pakistan International Airlines can be carried forward for ten years.  (All provisions are in Section 57.)

rows.answer: The deductible allowance can be claimed by any individual who pays tuition fees and whose taxable income is less than Rs 1.5 million in the tax year, and it may be taken by either parent who actually makes the payment provided the parent furnishes his/her NTN or the name of the educational institution. The allowance is limited to the lesser of (i) 5 % of the total tuition fee paid, (ii) 25 % of the individual’s taxable income, or (iii) Rs 60,000 multiplied by the number of the individual’s children, and any unused portion cannot be carried forward. (Tax year 2027 onward)

rows.answer: Yes. Under Section 61 of the Income Tax Ordinance, a donation to a public university that is established by Federal or Provincial law qualifies for a tax credit for the donor in tax year 2027 [1]. The credit is calculated using the formula in subsection (2), where the amount of credit (C) is the lesser of the total donation (must be paid by a crossed cheque) or 30 % of the donor’s taxable income (for an individual) [1]. The credit is then applied against the tax assessed after other credits, as per the same provision [1].

rows.answer: Yes. For tax year 2027 an individual can claim a tax credit for profit on debt (interest) paid on a loan from a scheduled bank or other regulated institution that is used to construct or acquire a personal house (up to 2,500 sq ft land or 2,000 sq ft flat). The credit is calculated as (A/B) × C where A is the tax assessed before any credit, B is taxable income, and C is the lesser of the total profit on debt paid or 30 % of taxable income; the credit is unavailable for profit deductible under section 15A and only one claim is allowed per individual for the next fifteen tax years[1].

rows.answer: Under the Income Tax Ordinance a "tax year" (normal tax year) is a period of twelve months ending on 30 June and is denoted by the calendar year in which that date falls [1]. A person may be allowed to use a different twelve‑month period as a special tax year, either by a Board notification or by a Commissioner’s order, and that special year is likewise identified by the calendar year of its closing date [1]. The definition is restated in the definitions clause, which includes both normal and special tax years [3].

rows.answer: An individual must be present in Pakistan for at least 183 days (or more) in aggregate during the tax year to be classified as a resident individual.

rows.answer: Yes. Under Section 82 a Pakistani citizen is a resident individual for tax year 2027 if he is present in Pakistan for an aggregate of at least 183 days in the tax year, counting each day of arrival, departure and certain holidays as a full day (Rule 14) and provided he is not present in any other country for more than 182 days or a resident taxpayer elsewhere [1, 3]. Additionally, a citizen who is an employee or official of the Federal or Provincial Government posted abroad also qualifies as a resident individual regardless of physical presence [1].

rows.answer: A company is a resident company for a tax year if it meets any one of the following conditions: (a) it is incorporated or formed under any law in force in Pakistan; (b) the control and management of its affairs are situated wholly in Pakistan at any time during the year; or (c) it is a Provincial Government or a Local Government in Pakistan[1]. This definition is reflected in the Ordinance’s definition of “resident company”[3].

rows.answer: For tax year 2027, a resident individual’s foreign‑source salary is exempt from Pakistani tax if the individual has paid foreign income tax on that salary (or the tax was withheld by the foreign employer and remitted to the foreign revenue authority). If no foreign tax has been paid, the salary would be taxable in Pakistan. [2]

rows.answer: For tax year 2027 the foreign tax credit on foreign‑source income is limited to the lesser of (a) the foreign income tax actually paid (including foreign withholding tax) and (b) the Pakistan tax payable on that income, which is calculated by applying the taxpayer’s average Pakistan income‑tax rate for the year to the net foreign‑source income (after allowable deductions) [1]. The credit is computed separately for each head of income, must be claimed within two years of the tax year, and cannot be refunded or carried forward/back [1].

rows.answer: For tax year 2027, salary is Pakistan‑source income if it is received from any employment exercised in Pakistan, wherever it is paid, or if it is paid by, or on behalf of, the Federal Government, a Provincial Government or a Local Government in Pakistan, wherever the employment is exercised [1].

rows.answer: If you cannot provide a satisfactory explanation for the nature and source of an investment, money, valuable article or the funds used for an expenditure, the amount is deemed to be part of your taxable income. It is included under the head “Income from Other Sources” (or under “Income from Business” for suppressed production or sales) and taxed in the year to which the amount relates if it is Pakistan‑source, or in the preceding tax year if it is foreign‑source and discovered later [1, 2]. An amount of foreign exchange remitted through normal banking channels up to Rs 5 million in a tax year with a bank certificate is excluded from this provision [2]. The Commissioner may also add any shortfall between the declared cost and a reasonable cost of the investment or expenditure to income from other sources [2].

rows.answer: For tax year 2027, section 113 (minimum tax) applies to a resident company, a permanent establishment of a non‑resident company, an individual whose turnover is Rs 100 million or more in FY 2017 or any later year, and an association of persons whose turnover is Rs 100 million or more in FY 2017 or any later year, where for any reason the tax payable is nil or less than the percentage of turnover specified in the First Schedule [1]. The provision does not apply to persons specifically exempted in Second Schedule Part IV clause 11A, such as taxpayers in the most‑affected Khyber Pakhtunkhwa/FATA/PATA areas (excluding certain manufacturers), rice mills (FY 2015), entities qualifying for exemptions under clauses 126I‑126O (renewable‑energy equipment, warehousing, halal meat, etc.), certain government bodies, petroleum dealers (except those operating petrol pumps), Hub Power Company, companies exempt under clause 126M, and several other listed entities [3, 4, 6]. Distributors, dealers, sub‑dealers and wholesalers of specified goods may pay a reduced minimum‑tax rate of 0.5% if they appear on the active taxpayers’ list, but they remain subject to the minimum‑tax regime [5].

rows.answer: For tax year 2027, a return of income must be furnished by (a) every company [1]. (ab) Every person (other than a company) whose taxable income for the year exceeds the maximum amount that is not chargeable to tax under the Ordinance [1]. (ac) Any non‑profit organization as defined in clause (36) of section 2 [1]. (ae) Every person whose income for the year is subject to final taxation under any provision of the Ordinance [1]. (b) Any person not covered by the preceding categories who (i) has been charged to tax in either of the two preceding tax years, or (ii) claims a loss carried forward, or (iii) owns immovable property of at least five hundred square yards, or (iv) owns a flat of at least two thousand square feet, or (v) owns a motor vehicle with engine capacity above 1000 cc, or (vi) has obtained a National Tax Number, or (vii) has a commercial/industrial electricity connection with an annual bill exceeding Rs 500,000, or (viii) is a resident person registered with a chamber of commerce, professional body or similar association, or (ix) is a resident individual required to file a foreign income and assets statement under section 116A [1]. (c) Any persons or classes of persons notified by the Board with the approval of the Minister in‑charge [1]. (1A) Every individual whose income under the head “Income from business” exceeds Rs 300,000 but does not exceed Rs 400,000 in a tax year [1]. Persons such as widows, orphans below 25 years, disabled persons, and non‑resident owners of immovable property are specifically exempt from filing a return [3].

rows.answer: Under section 116, the Commissioner may, by written notice, require a resident individual filing a return of income to furnish a wealth statement in the prescribed form and verified manner. The statement must disclose (a) the person’s total assets and liabilities, including foreign assets and liabilities, as on the specified date(s); (b) the total assets of the person’s spouse (if dependent), minor children and other dependents; (c) any assets transferred by the person during the period and the consideration received; (d) the total expenditures incurred by the person, spouse, minor children and other dependents and details of such expenditures; and (e) a reconciliation statement of wealth. [1]

rows.answer: To obtain more time you must submit a written application to the Commissioner before the return’s due date, explaining a reasonable cause such as absence from Pakistan, sickness or any other reasonable reason. If satisfied, the Commissioner may grant an extension of up to fifteen days, and in exceptional circumstances a longer period may be allowed. If the Commissioner does not grant an extension, you may apply to the Chief Commissioner for a further extension of up to fifteen days, again only unless exceptional circumstances justify a longer period. The granted extension does not alter the due date for payment of tax. (Tax year 2027)

rows.answer: The Commissioner may amend an original assessment order only within five years after the end of the financial year in which the original assessment was issued or treated as issued (Section 122(2)). If the assessment has already been amended, a further amendment is permitted only within the later of (a) five years from the end of the financial year of the original assessment, or (b) one year from the end of the financial year in which the most recent amended assessment was issued (Section 122(4)). Any amendment must be made under the conditions set out in Section 122(5) – e.g., where income has escaped assessment, total income was under‑assessed, excessive relief was given, etc. (Section 122(5)).
